slides.title: Most marketers use AI
slides.body: AI can take whole chunks of your week. Here are 5 tasks you can hand over today, with a good tool for each.

slides.title: Task 1: First drafts of captions
slides.body: Give it your post idea, audience and tone. Ask for 10 hooks, pick one, then edit it in your own words.

slides.title: Task 2: Summarise long documents
slides.body: Paste a client brief or meeting notes. Ask for key decisions, open questions and next steps in a table.

slides.title: Task 3: Research a topic fast
slides.body: Ask for an overview with sources. Open and check every source yourself before you use a fact.

slides.title: Task 4: Resize one design
slides.body: Design one post, then resize it for Story, Reel cover and LinkedIn instead of designing four times.

slides.title: Task 5: Draft replies to DMs
slides.body: List your 10 most common questions. Ask AI for short, friendly replies and save them as quick replies.

hook_options: Don't raise your ad budget yet

slides.hook_sub: 4 fixes to check before you raise your budget
slides.visual: B+D cover: glass headline, Meta + Instagram + WhatsApp stickers

slides.title: More budget won't fix
slides.body: If people click but don't enquire, the problem is usually after the click. Fix these 4 things first, then scale.

slides.title: Fix 1: The page is slow
slides.body: Open your landing page on mobile data. If the offer isn't clear at first glance, rewrite the top section.

slides.title: Fix 2: Too many form fields
slides.body: Name and phone are often enough to start. Ask the rest on the call. Each extra field adds friction.

slides.title: Fix 3: Slow replies
slides.body: A lead who waits hours may have moved on. Set up an instant reply on WhatsApp or DM, then follow up.

slides.title: Fix 4: A vague offer
slides.body: 'Best services in town' says nothing. Say what they get, who it's for and the price range in ₹.

slides.cta_body: Comment "AI" and I'll DM you the 4-point checklist.
slides.visual: glass card, Comment AI pill, stickers

posts.caption:
Facebook ads getting clicks but no leads? Check these 4 things first.

It's tempting to raise the budget when leads are low. But if people are clicking and still not enquiring, more budget just buys more of the same problem. The leak is usually after the click: a confusing page, a long form, slow replies or an offer that says nothing.

Go through the 4 fixes on your own ad this week.

Comment "AI" and I'll DM you my lead-leak checklist.

posts.linkedin_post:
Clicks but no leads is rarely a budget problem.

Before scaling, check what happens after the click:
1. Is the offer clear at first glance on mobile?
2. Are you asking for more form fields than you need?
3. How fast does a new lead get a reply?
4. Does the offer say what they get, for whom, and the price range?

Fix the leak, then scale.

posts.caption:
How to use AI for content without sounding like AI.

The problem isn't the tool. It's posting the first draft. Add one real example from your work, rewrite it the way you talk and check every number before you post.

Save this for the next time you open ChatGPT.
